Proactive fleet hedging and remediation protocol for dedicated capacity shortfalls

Summary:
We need a formalized protocol (hedging + remediation) to reduce customer impact during dedicated capacity shortfalls and autoscaling regressions. This ticket captures the incident chronology, short-term mitigations we executed, hypotheses for root causes, and a prioritized action list for immediate and next-quarter engineering work.

Scope:
- Detection signals: enrich autoscaler telemetry, headroom and queue pressure metrics, and cross-check with request-level latency SLOs.
- Immediate mitigations: non-disruptive hedges (burst routing to hosted pool, per-tenant throttles) and safe rollback patterns.
- Long-term controls: pre-warm headroom hedges, autoscaler guardrails, and escape hatches for fleet controllers.
- Documentation and runbook updates, plus postmortem RCA and follow-ups.

Background / Motivation:
A series of dedicated-pool incidents in Q4–Q1 exposed gaps where scaling regressions combined with aggressive bin-packing and a late kernel rollout caused headroom collapse. Customers saw degraded throughput and failed requests during peak bursts; our temporary mitigations were effective but manual and slow. We need a repeatable protocol that can be executed automatically or with a single operator decision.

Detection timeline (high level):
- 2025-02-14 09:12 UTC: Alert — dedicated-pool queue-latency p95 > 2.5s.
- 2025-02-14 09:18 UTC: Autoscaler flapping observed when pods rebalanced after a kernel update.
- 2025-02-14 09:32 UTC: Manual mitigation — route lower-priority customers to hosted fallback; reduced error rate but increased cost.
- 2025-02-14 12:00 UTC: Stabilized after rolling back the kernel and increasing per-pool min replicas.

Immediate mitigations executed during the incident:
- Deployed temporary routing rule to shard <10% traffic to hosted API for affected tenants (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/7342).
- Raised per-pool min-replicas from 3 to 5 for critical pools.
- Disabled the new kernel rollout and pinned kernel-version v1.18.3.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
- A combination of subtle scheduler/placement changes in the new kernel and a recent autoscaler tuning reduced reactive headroom. Continuous batching with longer tails increased memory pressure leading to pod throttles and subsequent scale instability.

Design decisions & trade-offs considered:
- Conservative pre-warming of headroom vs. cost: pre-warming headroom by reserving 10% capacity reduces incident risk but increases committed cost.
- Strict per-tenant throttles vs. customer SLAs: throttles protect platform but must be tier-aware to avoid SLA violations for enterprise customers.
- Automated rollback triggers vs. false positives: automated rollback of kernel rollouts reduces time-to-stable but must be guarded against spurious metric spikes.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- Automated hedging policy implemented that can move a configurable fraction of traffic off dedicated pools within 2 minutes of a verified headroom collapse signal.
- Autoscaler guardrail feature that prevents min-replica decreases when queue pressure > threshold.
- Runbook updated with step-by-step mitigation and decision checklist; on-call can execute hedging action within 5 clicks or single CLI command.
- Postmortem completed with RCA and prioritized follow-ups assigned and scheduled.

Deliverables / Action items (owner / ETA):
- Hedging controller prototype (Luis Ortega) — 2025-03-14.
- Autoscaler guardrail design doc (Arjun Patel) — 2025-03-01 (doc: confluence.redwood.ai/display/Infra/Autoscaler+Guardrails).
- Runbook & CLI hedging command (Sofia Kline) — 2025-03-10 (runbook: drive.redwood.ai/Shared/Runbooks/dedicated-hedge.md).
- Cost-model for pre-warmed headroom (Finance + Product) — 2025-03-07 (dashboard: grafana/redwood/costs/dedicated-headroom).
- Postmortem and customer impact summary (Maya Chen) — 2025-03-05.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Over-eager hedging could route too much traffic to hosted pool and blow customer cost quotas. Mitigation: rate-limited hedges with tiered thresholds and automated rollback.
- Risk: Guardrails might prevent legitimate scale-downs, increasing idle cost. Mitigation: implement time-windowed guardrails and usage-aware decay.

Next steps (short-term):
1) Ship monitoring enrichment for headroom and queue shape (PR link: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/220).
2) Merge hedging controller prototype behind feature flag and run canary (alpha tenants) for 2 weeks.
3) Complete autoscaler guardrail RFC and review with SRE/Platform.
